messages:
sanjay: quick heads-up — i've been prototyping a different orchestration split: run a tiny sidecar per node that manages local warmup credits, KV cache hints, and short-lived admission tokens. want to chat tradeoffs before i write an RFC.

lucy: interesting. high-level win is lower central control-plane pressure?

sanjay: yeah. sidecar handles node-local decisions for prewarm and immediate admission; operator remains for long-lived contracts and shard placement. reduces rtt for admit checks.

dana: curious about consistency on eviction and global accounting — how do we avoid double-spending headroom across nodes?

sanjay: plan is tiered tokens: global leases for reserved capacity, local ephemeral tokens for burst. sidecar decrements ephemeral first; operator periodically reconciles and rebalances tokens.

marcus: reconciliation frequency is crucial. if operator runs every 30s we risk oversubscribe windows. can we keep a cheap vector clock or monotonic counter to bound races?

lucy: also need to think about failure modes: node sidecar crash, network partition, operator unavailable. What are safe fallbacks?

sanjay: fallback modes i sketched: 1) sidecar crash -> kube restarts, but node marks itself non-admit until sidecar returns. 2) operator unreachable -> sidecars switch to degraded conservative admission (50% headroom). 3) partition -> sidecars offer only local cached burst credits, no cross-node transfers.

tia: cost/fragmentation concern: local tokens could increase unutilized GPU time if bursts are hoarded. how do we reclaim?

sanjay: TTL on ephemeral tokens + decay policy; operator can force-drain ephemeral on sustained imbalance. reclaim events are rate-limited to avoid oscillation.

marcus: telemetry: we need per-sidecar metrics: ephemeral_tokens_in_use, stale_reconciles, forced_drains, last_sync_latency. add a tracing span for admit->response path.

lucy: agree. and expose an aggregate dimension so we can alert on global headroom skew.

dana: what about rollout complexity? sidecar requires image for all node types (gpu/non-gpu?). Also RBAC surface increases.

sanjay: sidecar will only run on gpu nodes as daemonset. RBAC is small: read/write to reservation CRDs and a token-check endpoint on operator. operator still owns reconciliation loop and policy config.

marcus: fallback for policy changes: we need canary toggles. suggest feature-flag that flips per-node admission behavior, and a control-plane switch to drain ephemeral pool before enabling new logic.

lucy: tests? simulation harness for high-churn admission patterns. add a chaos job that kills sidecars randomly to validate safety defaults.

tia: one more: prewarm cost accounting. breakdown per-tenant visible in billing — if sidecar prewarmed and got reclaimed, we still need to attribute cost correctly. operator must log transfer events.

sanjay: agreed. transfer events will be emitted as events with tags: tenant, node, reason. that'll feed billing pipeline.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary sidecar image tag redwood/orch-sidecar:v0.1 -> staging (3 nodes) — scheduled in 10m.

lucy: ok let's test in staging, run the chaos prewarm test, and collect metrics. i'll own the test plan.

dana: i'll draft a short RFC with failure modes matrix and the reconciliation algorithm pseudo-code.

marcus: i'll add the telemetry dashboard skeleton and alert rules.

tia: i'll write the billing events schema and an audit query.

sanjay: thanks — sync at 11:30 to review results. :thumbsup:
